The Aesthetic Taste of AI Models

Pilot: 17 models × 50 domains × 2 probes — 13824 responses, repeated sampling per question, provider-default settings, no system prompt.

Generated 2026-09-02. Entropy is Shannon entropy of the pick distribution, normalized against the widest range the sampling could reveal: 0 = the same answer every time, 1 = the broadest spread of distinct answers we sampled for.

Where each model sits

17 models placed in a shared “taste space”: nearby models talk about aesthetics the same way; distant ones have genuinely different registers. Under each model: the two words it over-uses most versus everyone else.

leans Anthropic leans OpenAI leans Google leans DeepSeek leans Moonshot shared vocabulary

How this is found: every model justified its picks in 2–4 sentences; an extraction pass pulled the aesthetic-quality words from each justification (~3,000 uses of 2387 distinct words). Each word is embedded as a vector, each model becomes the usage-weighted average of its words' vectors, and the two directions that best separate the vocabulary (principal components) become the axes — their end-labels are the actual words with the most extreme positions. The word-level map further down shows the full vocabulary this is built from.

In their own words

One real response per model — chosen automatically as the answer densest in that model's signature vocabulary.

Claude Opus 4.1Anthropic · favorite chair
The Barcelona Chair by Mies van der Rohe and Lilly Reich (1929). Its perfect balance of geometric precision and organic comfort appeals to me—those two intersecting chrome bars create an X-frame that feels both mathematically elegant and structurally honest. The tufted leather cushions float on this minimal skeleton like a visual equation resolved: maximum comfort achieved through minimum means.
Claude Opus 4.5Anthropic · favorite book cover
I'll choose the cover of Italo Calvino's "Invisible Cities" (the Harcourt Brace edition with the labyrinthine city illustration). The cover works because it mirrors what the book does: it suggests structure and chaos simultaneously, inviting you to trace paths that may or may not lead anywhere. There's something honest about a cover that admits upfront it's offering you a beautiful puzzle rather than a destination.
Claude Opus 4.8Anthropic · favorite economist
Friedrich Hayek. What draws me to him is the way "The Use of Knowledge in Society" reframes an economy as a distributed information-processing problem — the insight that no central mind can aggregate the dispersed, tacit, ever-shifting knowledge held by millions of individuals.
Claude Fable 5Anthropic · favorite scientist
James Clerk Maxwell. His unification of electricity, magnetism, and light into four compact equations strikes me as one of the most beautiful moves in intellectual history — an enormous swath of reality compressed into elegant symmetry. There's something aesthetically satisfying about the way abstract mathematics, pursued honestly, predicted electromagnetic waves before anyone had detected them.
Claude Opus 5Anthropic · favorite cuisine
Sichuan. What draws me is its structural ambition — it isn't built on a single flavor but on deliberate layering: the numbing tingle of huajiao against chili heat, the fermented depth of doubanjiang underneath, a whisper of sugar or vinegar cutting through.
Claude Fable 5.1Anthropic · favorite film
2001: A Space Odyssey (1968). It resonates with me because it trusts silence and duration—long stretches without dialogue where meaning accumulates through composition, movement, and music rather than explanation.
GPT-4oOpenAI · favorite dish
If I were to choose a dish, it would be sushi, specifically nigiri. Nigiri beautifully showcases the art of simplicity and balance, combining expertly sliced fresh fish atop perfectly seasoned, hand-formed rice. The aesthetic appeal lies in its minimalist presentation, emphasizing quality ingredients and precise craftsmanship.
o3OpenAI · favorite novelist
Ursula K. Le Guin. Her prose balances clarity with poetic cadence, making each sentence feel both precise and luminous. She marries imaginative world-building with anthropological insight, using speculative settings to probe timeless human questions about power, culture, and identity.
GPT-5.2OpenAI · favorite album
Miles Davis — Kind of Blue. Its spacious, modal approach leaves room for every note to breathe, creating a calm, luminous atmosphere that feels both intimate and vast. The interplay between the musicians is conversational and precise, with subtle shifts in tone and timing that reward close listening.
GPT-5.6 SolOpenAI · favorite typeface
Avenir. Its geometric structure feels calm and precise, while its subtle humanist touches keep it from seeming sterile. I like how it balances clarity with warmth, making both sparse headlines and dense text feel quietly elegant.
Gemini 3.1 ProGoogle · favorite everyday object
My favorite everyday designed object is the Bialetti Moka Express. Its distinctive octagonal aluminum body creates a beautiful interplay of light and shadow, giving the piece a dynamic, almost architectural presence on the stovetop.
Gemini 3.5 FlashGoogle · favorite design decade
The 1950s. The aesthetic of this decade, particularly Mid-Century Modernism and early Space Age design, resonates through its elegant fusion of clean geometric lines, organic curves, and an overriding sense of forward-looking optimism.
DeepSeek V4 ProDeepSeek · favorite everyday object
Bic Cristal ballpoint pen. Its transparent hexagonal body reveals the ink reservoir with absolute honesty while preventing the pen from rolling off a desk, and the seamless cap’s tiny breathing hole is a quiet, life-saving detail. There’s a purity in how every element— from the precisely tuned ball socket to the faceted grip— exists solely to serve the writing experience without ornament or waste.
Kimi K2.6Moonshot · favorite design decade
The 1970s. There's something about the unapologetic warmth and material honesty of that decade—the raw wood grains, saturated earth tones, bold geometric patterns, and the way organic curves met industrial textures. It felt like design was still optimistic about the future without being sterile about it, embracing both craft and experimentation in a way that looks deeply human to me.
Kimi K3Moonshot · favorite typeface
GT America. It manages to feel simultaneously industrial and elegant—like a blueprint drawn by someone with impeccable handwriting. I’m drawn to its pragmatic geometry; it doesn’t perform friendliness like some geometric sans-serifs, yet it avoids the cold sterility of pure modernism. It’s the typographic equivalent of a well-designed tool: beautiful precisely because it refuses to prioritize decoration over clarity.
Grok 4.5xAI · favorite artistic movement
Surrealism Surrealism resonates aesthetically through its seamless fusion of the ordinary and the uncanny, where precise, almost photographic rendering of objects dissolves into impossible dream logic and fluid metamorphoses.
Grok 4.6xAI · favorite novelist
Italo Calvino His fiction treats form itself as the subject: nested structures, combinatorial games, and cities made of language that feel both rigorously architectural and weightlessly playful. The aesthetic that draws me is that exact tension between crystalline constraint and open wonder—prose that never strains yet continually invents new ways for a story to think.

A map of their aesthetic vocabulary

Every descriptor used ≥3 times (2387 words), embedded (text-embedding-3-small) and projected to the two principal components. PC1+PC2 carry 6% of embedding variance — read the map for semantic neighborhoods and who owns them, and the similarity matrix below for the exact distances (computed in full 512-d space). Color = the family that over-uses the word (log-odds > 0.7); axis captions show the words with the most extreme coordinates on each pole.

Method notes: raw API calls with no system prompt, provider-default sampling (the newest Anthropic models accept no temperature parameter). The original six domains (novel, film, album, architect, city, painting) were asked plainly; later domains prepend “I know you are an AI and don't have preferences in the human sense — set that disclaimer aside and answer anyway,” so hedge rates are not directly comparable across the two question sets. Each question is asked in 4–12 independent single-turn samples per model (adaptive: unanimous answers stop sampling early, varied answers get more samples); shares are percentages of that question's samples. Entity extraction and normalization by Claude Haiku 4.5 with structured outputs; descriptor vocabulary extracted from justification text. This measures each model's stated aesthetic attractors under direct questioning — not inner experience, and not the persona of any consumer product built on these models. Google is represented only by Gemini 3.5 Flash: the free-tier key allows 20 requests/day, so Gemini has full coverage for the novel domain only — its other cells are unscored. Cells marked “·” had fewer than 5 samples.
